security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder HTTPS URLs, or documented CLI credential storage. Confirmed issues are expected operational risks: the skill installs or runs the RunComfy CLI and sends prompts and image references to RunComfy infrastructure. No evidence found for prompt injection, arbitrary command injection, path traversal, or credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and package installation
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running npm, npx, or runcomfy commands, and pin the RunComfy CLI version when practical.
Tell users that prompts and image URLs are processed by RunComfy, and advise against sensitive or private images unless that processing is approved.
Document token storage, file permissions, token rotation, and use of RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI or container environments.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image edit workflows can drift when prompts do not protect identity, framing, or brand details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical RunComfy workflow for targeted Nano Banana 2 edits.
actual_capabilities: Explains the google/nano-banana-2/edit input fields and supported output settings.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for single-image, batch, and spatially targeted edits.
Guides prompts that preserve subject identity, pose, clothing, brand details, and framing.
Compares Nano Banana Edit with GPT Image 2 edit, Flux Kontext, and Nano Banana 2 text-to-image.
Documents limits, exit codes, outbound endpoints, and token storage behavior.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.
Requires publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs for input images.
Sends prompts and image references to RunComfy model infrastructure.
Long compound edits can drift and may need multiple passes.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Galleries
use_cases.description: Create consistent background swaps for product images while preserving product shape, label details, and framing.

use_cases.title: Adapt Campaign Creatives
use_cases.description: Generate controlled ad variants with locked aspect ratio, stable subject identity, and repeatable prompt structure.

use_cases.title: Localize Visual Assets
use_cases.description: Replace a specific label, object, or background area while keeping the rest of the composition unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this image with Nano Banana Edit. Keep the subject identity, pose, clothing, and framing unchanged. Replace only the background with a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Product Batch Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit for these product images. Keep each product, label, angle, and scale unchanged. Apply the same neutral background and lock the aspect ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Targeted Object Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit only the object in the upper-right area. Keep the main subject, lighting, background, and all other objects exactly as shown.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Pass Brand Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a two-pass Nano Banana Edit workflow. First preserve identity while changing the background. Then update the clothing color without changing the face or pose.

output_examples.input: A portrait needs a new studio background without changing the person or clothing.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a preservation-first prompt and a RunComfy Nano Banana Edit call using one public image URL.

output_examples.input: A team wants ten product photos to share the same background and square framing.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a batch edit, locked aspect ratio, fixed resolution, and repeated prompt grammar across all inputs.

output_examples.input: A label in one part of an image needs replacement while the rest stays unchanged.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a spatially scoped instruction that names the exact area, retained elements, and replacement text.

best_practices: Lead every edit prompt with the details that must stay unchanged.
Use concrete spatial language for local edits, such as background only or upper-right corner.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing a batch of related images.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edit goals in one prompt.
Do not use private or sensitive image URLs unless RunComfy processing is acceptable.
Do not omit preservation goals when faces, products, logos, or labels must remain stable.

faq.question: What model does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the google/nano-banana-2/edit endpoint through the local RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it generate images from scratch?
faq.answer: No. This skill is for image-to-image editing from one or more existing image URLs.

faq.question: How many input images can it handle?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint accepts 1 to 20 input images per call.

faq.question: Can it keep a person or product unchanged?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes preservation-first prompts for identity, pose, clothing, product shape, and framing.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need the RunComfy CLI and either browser login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Where does processing happen?
faq.answer: The CLI submits requests to RunComfy model infrastructure and downloads generated outputs from RunComfy URLs.
